name: Ngwe
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

sources.citation: Nguendjio, Emile-Gille. 1992. Temps et aspect de la langue bangwa. Journal of West African Languages 22(2): 89-100.
sources.note: NOT Ngwe: 'langue du sous-groupe nda'nda' (Province de l'Ouest)', ALCAM code 980. Tense/aspect and tone; no stress. Identity warning only.

sources.citation: Chumbow, Beban Sammy & Emile Gille Nguendjio. 1991. Floating tones in Bangwa. Journal of West African Languages 21(1).
sources.note: NOT Ngwe: p. 1 'Bangwa is an Eastern Grassfield language spoken in the Nde Division of the West Province of Cameroon' (Mbam-Nkam, Nda'nda' subgroup). Tone only. Kept as an identity warning; not used.

sources.citation: Dunstan, Elizabeth. 1964. Towards a phonology of Ngwe. Journal of West African Languages 1(1): 39-42.
sources.access_detail: copy on file; access check: online with a university library login (also: harvard online access (harvardkey))
sources.note: Nothing. Consonant/vowel inventory, allophones, word list with tones marked high/mid/low (p. 40); closes 'It appears that there are three tonemes in Ngwe, but this needs further investigation' (p. 42). Word 'stress'/'accent' absent.
Vowel inventory only (cites Ladefoged 1968: 33-36); no information on tone or stress.

sources.citation: Nkemnji, Michael. 1994. On Nweh adjectives that show up as nouns. Paper, 25th Annual Conference on African Linguistics, New Brunswick NJ. ERIC ED374669, 20 pp.
sources.note: Nothing; syntax paper. Only a footnote on tone change and a lengthened final nasal 'considered tonal rather than' segmental.

sources.citation: Dunstan, Elizabeth. 1966. Tone on disyllabic nouns in Ngwe. Journal of West African Languages 3(1): 33-38.
sources.note: Nothing. Three tonal classes of disyllabic nouns (prefix + stem), tone changes in subject/object position, low fall before pause, extra-high pitch; no stress/accent anywhere.
38 segments; no tones listed; no mention of stress.
